queries.rationale: Gather work on mapping operator intent (NL) to device/router configs, including systems, datasets, and evaluation practices.
Identify architectures combining generation with deterministic validators or repair loops (generate→validate→repair) and concrete validators applicable to network configs.

queries.query: formal verification network configurations "reachability" "policy compliance" "header space" "model checking"
queries.rationale: Collect foundational and recent work on formal/deterministic verification of network behavior to use as validators or ground truth in NetOps experiments.

industry blog posts only if accompanied by reproducible code

inclusion_criteria: Primary research papers (conference or journal) and archival preprints (arXiv) with verifiable bibliographic metadata
Tool and validator project pages and repositories with public artifacts or documentation (GitHub, Zenodo)
Empirical studies, reproducible experiments, or method descriptions relevant to NetOps, verification, AIOps, or LLM tool use
Recent work (preferentially within the last 3 years for LLM-specific methods; include older foundational work for verification and networking)
Work that provides metrics, datasets, code, or clear methodological descriptions enabling reproducible assessment
exclusion_criteria: Private, NDA-restricted, or paywalled artifacts that cannot be accessed for verification
Purely opinion pieces or marketing material without empirical or methodological substance, unless corroborated by reproducible artifacts
Benchmarks or papers unrelated to operational correctness, safety, or NetOps (e.g., purely language-only benchmarks without NetOps applicability)
Sources lacking verifiable authorship, title, venue, or stable identifier
date_rationale: Cover foundational literature historically (formal verification, network tools) and prioritize recent work (last 3 years) for LLM-specific methods and agentic NetOps due to rapid progress; target coverage up to the submission window (through 2026-08) while ensuring primary-source verification for each citation.
